newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chess prodigy Kamsky says retires at 22 - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Chess prodigy Kamsky says retires at 22 - Tass.

text.p: Russian-born chess prodigy Gata Kamsky, defeated in his challenge for the FIDE world chess championship last July, has decided to retire from top-level competitive chess, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.
Tass quoted the 22-year-old Kamsky as saying he would never have a realistic chance at the world chess title and wanted to catch up on his lost education and maybe become a doctor.

"It has been clear for some time that Anatoly Karpov and Garry Kasparov will do all they can not to allow any of the possible pretenders to sit on the world chess throne," he told Tass in an interview from New York, where he has lived since leaving the Soviet Union with his father at the age of 15.
Russians Karpov and Kasparov are respectively leading lights in the world's rival chess organisations, the long-established FIDE and the breakaway Professional Chess Association.
The two bodies took steps to defuse emnity between them late last year. Kasparov is regarded as the unofficial world number one.

Kamsky, 22, lost to the experienced Karpov in last July's $2 million challenge for the FIDE world championship. It was held in Elista, capital of the autonomous Russian region of Kalmykia, whose president is FIDE chief Kirsan Ilyumzhinov.

At the age of just 12, Kamsky won the Soviet under-20 chess title. He emigrated to the United States three years later and, driven relentlessly by his ambitious father Rustam, he won the full U.S. championship at the age of 16.
He was the first American to challenge for the official world title since Bobby Fischer beat Boris Spassky in 1972 to record what was a notable propaganda victory in the Cold War.
Tass quoted Kamsky as saying he now wanted to catch up on the education he neglected during 10 years of intensive chess.

"I am going to college and I hope to go to university in two years," he said. "I have not yet made up my mind what my future profession will be, but I am attracted above all by medicine and chemistry."
